[LTIM.7.3] **`floor` consults no timezone, so a DST transition moves no
boundary.** A `Time` carries an offset, not a zone ([LTIM.1.1.1]), and `floor`
truncates at that offset ([LTIM.7.1]). For a receiver resolved in a zone that
observes DST:

- **Spring-forward.** A receiver resolved after the transition carries the new
  offset, so flooring it to `1_d` returns midnight at that offset, an hour
  before the zone's own midnight on the transition day. America/Los_Angeles,
  2026-03-08: 12:00 at −7 h floors to 00:00 at −7 h (07:00Z); the zone's
  midnight that day is 00:00 at −8 h (08:00Z).
- **Fall-back.** The second 1:30 AM carries the standard offset, so flooring it
  to `1_h` returns 1:00 at that offset, the second 1 AM rather than the first.
  America/Los_Angeles, 2026-11-01: 1:30 at −8 h floors to 1:00 at −8 h
  (09:00Z).

An author who wants a zone's own boundary floors a value resolved with
`.local(tz)` at an instant on the same side of the transition as that
boundary.
